title: Consider adding a matching runtime enum/allowed-key source shared between hando…
description:
Consider adding a matching runtime enum/allowed-key source shared between handoff.schema.json and OFFICIAL_DOCS_VALIDATED_STATUSES/ALLOWED_KEYS in events.ts to prevent future drift; today they are hand-synced in two places.

Source: cam/issue-229
Review round: 1
Location: scripts/cam/handoff.schema.json

suggestion-fingerprint: cf72f51d0714

acceptanceCriteria: src/supervisor/events.ts imports scripts/cam/handoff.schema.json and derives OFFICIAL_DOCS_VALIDATED_STATUSES from the schema's officialDocsValidated items status.enum, and OFFICIAL_DOCS_VALIDATED_ALLOWED_KEYS from Object.keys of that item's properties. The hand-maintained literal arrays are removed.
handoff.schema.json is the single source of truth: changing the status enum or the item's property set in the schema alone updates the runtime validator with no second edit.
'resolveJsonModule': true is added to tsconfig.json compilerOptions so tsc --noEmit accepts the JSON import.

OFFICIAL_DOCS_VALIDATED_STATUSES is still usable as a readonly string[] at the .includes(status) call site (line ~613); no consumer relies on a literal-union type (verified: the only use casts to readonly string[]).
validateOfficialDocsValidated behavior is unchanged: same statuses accepted, same allowed keys, warn-only, one-entry-one-warning contract preserved.
The 'Source of truth: ... handoff.schema.json' comments are updated to reflect that the values are now derived from the schema, not hand-copied.
typecheck and the full test suite pass green; the cam binary still builds (bun build --compile inlines the JSON import).
spec.scope: Remove the hand-synced duplication of the officialDocsValidated status enum and allowed-key set between scripts/cam/handoff.schema.json and src/supervisor/events.ts by making the schema the single source: events.ts imports and derives both. Touch src/supervisor/events.ts and tsconfig.json (resolveJsonModule). No behavior change.
gotchas: handoff.schema.json is NOT read at runtime today (no ajv, no schema parse); events.ts validates with hand-coded consts. This change makes the schema authoritative by importing it. Do not confuse it with src/orchestrator/handoff.ts, which is the DIFFERENT orch-handoff schema.
tsconfig has module:Preserve + moduleResolution:bundler but no resolveJsonModule; add resolveJsonModule:true or tsc --noEmit will error on the JSON import.

The import path from src/supervisor/events.ts is ../../scripts/cam/handoff.schema.json (a committed contract artifact under the data dir); bun build --compile inlines it, so there is no runtime file dependency.

Deriving ALLOWED_KEYS via Object.keys(items.properties) matches the additionalProperties:false intent and auto-tracks any property added to the schema — this is the drift-prevention the SUGGESTION asked for; no separate drift test is needed because there is now only one source.
